links.outcome: Detection of data drift and performance degradation in deployed mortality model
links.effect: Label-agnostic pipeline detected shifts (age groups, admission source, hospital type, BNP, D-dimer); shifts led to reduced AUROC/AUPRC overall and across subgroups.
links.quote: We observed that the identified data shifts led to reduced AUROC, AUPRC, or both for the overall population (eFigure 6 in Supplement 1 ) and across subgroups (eFigure 7 in Supplement 1 ).

links.outcome: Model performance with drift-triggered updating versus locked model during COVID-19
links.effect: Data shift-triggered continual updating improved performance over a locked model during COVID-19 (Delta AUROC [SD], 0.44 [0.02]; P = .007, Mann-Whitney U test).
links.quote: Overall, data shift–triggered continual updating improved model performance over time and was more effective than maintaining a locked model during the COVID-19 pandemic (Delta AUROC [SD], 0.44 [0.02]; P = .007, Mann-Whitney U test) ( Figure 4 B).

links.outcome: Performance gain from fine-tuning/transfer learning on target hospital data
links.effect: Community hospitals benefited from community-specific pretraining (Delta AUROC 0.05 [0.03]; Delta AUPRC 0.06 [0.04]); hospital type-specific fine-tuning improved all sites except hospital 2.
links.quote: Hospital type–specific fine-tuning improved performance for all sites except hospital 2, where ablating hospital 3 yielded the best performance.

links.outcome: Performance change when model transferred between hospital types
links.effect: Community-to-academic transfer decreased performance for patients aged 65 or older (Delta AUROC -0.05; Delta AUPRC -0.02) and gave mixed results for younger patients.
links.quote: Transferring from community to academic hospitals led to decreased model performance for patients aged 65 or older (Delta AUROC [SD], −0.05 [0.003]; Delta AUPRC [SD], −0.02 [0.01]) and to mixed results for younger patients (Delta AUROC [SD], 0.07 [0.02]; Delta AUPRC [SD], −0.26 [0.02]).

links.outcome: Model performance across diagnostic, age, and sex subgroups
links.effect: Performance was lower for neoplasms (AUROC 0.77) and health status factors (AUROC 0.75) than circulatory (0.86) or infectious diseases (0.87); varied by age, consistent across sex.
links.quote: Performance varied by age but remained consistent across sex ( Figure 1 D).

links.outcome: Drift-triggered versus fixed-interval model updating performance
links.effect: Data shift-triggered model updating improved performance compared with updating at fixed intervals; best P value threshold .01.
links.quote: To mitigate model deterioration, we leveraged continual learning ( Figure 4 A) and found that data shift–triggered model updating improved performance compared with updating at fixed intervals (eFigure 9 in Supplement 1 ).

links.outcome: Label-agnostic drift detection
links.effect: Detected shifts from younger age/admission source, community-to-academic transfer, and BNP/D-dimer changes.
links.quote: Significant data shifts were detected as a result of changes in younger age groups and admissions from nursing homes and acute care centers, transferring from community to academic hospitals, and changes in brain natriuretic peptide and D-dimer.

links.outcome: Drift-triggered continual updating
links.effect: Compared with locked model during COVID-19: Delta AUROC [SD], 0.44 [0.02]; P = .007.
links.quote: Overall, data shift–triggered continual updating improved model performance over time and was more effective than maintaining a locked model during the COVID-19 pandemic (Delta AUROC [SD], 0.44 [0.02]; P = .007, Mann-Whitney U test) ( Figure 4 B).

links.outcome: Transfer learning for local adaptation
links.effect: Community hospitals: Delta AUROC [SD], 0.05 [0.03]; Delta AUPRC [SD], 0.06 [0.04], hospital type-dependent.
links.quote: Transfer learning improved model performance of community hospitals in a hospital type-dependent manner (Delta AUROC [SD], 0.05 [0.03]; Delta AUPRC [SD], 0.06 [0.04]).

links.outcome: Cross-setting dataset shift
links.effect: Community-to-academic transfer decreased age ≥65 AUROC −0.05 [0.003] and AUPRC −0.02 [0.01]; younger AUPRC −0.26 [0.02].
links.quote: Transferring from community to academic hospitals led to decreased model performance for patients aged 65 or older (Delta AUROC [SD], −0.05 [0.003]; Delta AUPRC [SD], −0.02 [0.01]) and to mixed results for younger patients (Delta AUROC [SD], 0.07 [0.02]; Delta AUPRC [SD], −0.26 [0.02]).

links.outcome: Subgroup performance gaps
links.effect: Worse for neoplasms AUROC 0.77 [0.02], AUPRC 0.42 [0.03]; health status AUROC 0.75 [0.02], AUPRC 0.63 [0.04].
links.quote: The model performed best for circulatory system diseases (AUROC for code groups I00-I99 [SD], 0.86 [0.01]; AUPRC for code groups I00-I99 [SD], 0.38 [0.01]), respiratory system diseases (AUROC for code groups J00-J99 [SD], 0.82 [0.01]; AUPRC for code groups J00-J99 [SD], 0.43 [0.04]), and infectious and parasitic diseases (AUROC for code groups A00-B99 [SD], 0.87 [0.01]; AUPRC for code groups A00-B99 [SD], 0.45 [0.02]), but it performed worse for neoplasms (AUROC for code groups C00-D49 [SD], 0.77 [0.02]; AUPRC for code groups C00-D49 [SD], 0.42 [0.03]) and health status factors (AUROC for code groups Z00-Z99 [SD], 0.75 [0.02]; AUPRC for code groups Z00-Z99 [SD], 0.63 [0.04]), which primarily consisted of patients receiving palliative care (n = 2042).

screen.practice: drift monitoring and triggered continual learning
screen.reason: The study develops and directly evaluates a post-deployment safeguarding practice: a proactive data drift monitoring pipeline coupled with drift-triggered continual learning and transfer learning to prevent model degradation in clinical EHR risk prediction.
